speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having blisters on your forearm and ulcers on mucosal surfaces; can you tell me exactly where these ulcers are located and how long you have had these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS)

I have noted your recent history of taking captopril and your family history of autoimmune conditions. Given the combination of blisters on the forearm and painful mucosal ulcers in the mouth and genital area, this presentation is highly suspicious for a severe drug reaction. Could you confirm if any new medications were started within the last two months, and do you have a fever or feel generally unwell?
